findings.motion: HB 958 Election Law Changes, Second Reading (roll call 758, passed 66-47)
findings.note: Recorded as voting No on second reading of HB 958. The ratified text bars processing a voter registration application unless the applicant states they are a US citizen, requires a signed statement under penalty of perjury about citizenship when the question is left blank, and orders the State Board of Elections to set up a process to remove voters flagged as possible non-citizens by a federal database.
subjects: proof of citizenship to register
non-citizen voting and voter-roll checks
election integrity law in general

findings.motion: HB 834 State Board of Elections Administrative Changes, M11 Concur (roll call 800, passed 74-35; became SL 2026-60)
findings.note: Recorded as voting No on concurrence in HB 834. The session law moves the deadline to cure ballot problems to the fifth business day after the election, including bringing photo ID after a provisional ballot cast without it, supplying an ID photocopy or affidavit with an absentee ballot, and fixing mismatched ID numbers. Text: https://www.ncleg.gov/Sessions/2025/Bills/House/PDF/H834v6.pdf.

findings.motion: Co-sponsor of HB 1246 Safeguarding Elections Act (listed in her Introduced Bills page at https://www.ncleg.gov/Members/IntroducedBills/H/832)
findings.note: Rep. Helfrich is listed among the sponsors of HB 1246 (primary sponsor another member). Among other provisions, the filed text makes it a Class 2 misdemeanor for any person to demand citizenship documentation from a voter other than what State law requires at any point during the voting process (draft text: https://www.ncleg.gov/Sessions/2025/Bills/House/PDF/H1246v0.pdf). The bill was referred to the Rules committee.
subjects: proof of citizenship to vote
election integrity law in general

findings.motion: HB 958, Election Law Changes, Second Reading (House roll call 758)
findings.note: Helfrich voted No on second reading of HB 958 (Election Law Changes); the vote was 66 Aye to 47 No. The ratified text (https://www.ncleg.gov/Sessions/2025/Bills/House/PDF/H958v9.pdf) adds a rule that a county board processes a voter registration application only if it states the applicant is a U.S. citizen, with a notice and a sworn statement under penalty of perjury if the answer is blank; it also orders a process to remove voters flagged as possible non-citizens by a federal database and sets list-maintenance changes. The vote-history page shows only her vote, not the reason.
subjects: proof of citizenship on a voter registration application
voter-roll checks against a federal database
election law changes in general
